themes_detail.label: For-Hire Vehicle Surge
themes_detail.summary: For-hire vehicle complaints (Uber, Lyft, etc.) spiked to 17 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 2.0 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 750% increase (z-score: 10.61)—suggesting rapid deterioration in traffic congestion, illegal parking, or passenger/driver conduct in Washington Heights/Inwood.
evidence: 17 for-hire vehicle complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (750% spike)
Z-score of 10.61 indicates statistically extreme deviation
372 active DOB permits filed in past 90 days suggest ongoing construction/street disruption may be channeling vehicles to residential areas
reporting_angles: Interview residents on residential blocks (e.g., Fort Washington Ave corridor) about increased congestion and illegal staging of ride-share vehicles
Obtain TLC data on complaints filed directly with Taxi & Limousine Commission for this week vs. baseline

themes_detail.label: Vendor Enforcement Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street vendor enforcement complaints jumped to 10 THIS WEEK compared to 1.9 per week baseline—a 433% increase (z-score: 5.29)—indicating either a sudden enforcement crackdown or a proliferation of unpermitted vendors triggering resident complaints.
evidence: 10 vendor enforcement complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.9 weekly average (433% spike)
Z-score of 5.29 indicates statistically significant anomaly
Community board has requested increased litter basket collection, suggesting street disorder is chronic concern
reporting_angles: Check with Department of Consumer Affairs on enforcement operations conducted THIS WEEK—any new compliance push?
Interview street vendors and residents on major commercial blocks (e.g., Broadway corridor) about visibility of enforcement

themes_detail.label: Dead/Dying Trees Spike
themes_detail.summary: Dead or dying tree complaints reached 4 LAST WEEK versus 0.1 per week baseline—a 3100% increase (z-score: 11.72)—potentially signaling climate stress, disease, or infrastructure damage in the district's aging tree canopy.
evidence: 4 dead/dying tree complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average (3100% spike)
Z-score of 11.72 is the highest statistical anomaly in dataset
Community board has repeatedly requested park upgrades and safety enhancements, suggesting parks maintenance is understaffed
reporting_angles: Map the 4 complaints to identify if trees are clustered in specific parks (e.g., Inwood Hill Park, Fort Tryon Park) or scattered
Contact NYC Parks on tree health assessments and whether recent weather (freeze-thaw cycles, storms) triggered die-off

themes_detail.label: Public Urination Spike
themes_detail.summary: Public urination complaints spiked to 3 LAST WEEK compared to 0.1 per week baseline—a 2300% increase (z-score: 8.69)—indicating either a concentrated street disorder issue or a cluster of homelessness-related incidents in a specific neighborhood area.
evidence: 3 public urination complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average (2300% spike)
Z-score of 8.69 indicates extreme statistical deviation
Converges with street/sidewalk noise complaints (2,712 over 90 days) and unsanitary conditions (1,332 over 90 days) suggesting broader street disorder
reporting_angles: Obtain geo-tagged 311 complaint locations to identify if incidents cluster on specific avenues or parks
Interview residents, storefront owners, and local precinct on whether this reflects a new encampment, inadequate public restroom access, or sudden behavioral shift

themes_detail.label: Smoking/Vaping in Public
themes_detail.summary: Smoking and vaping complaints rose to 11 TWO WEEKS AGO versus 4.0 per week baseline—a 175% increase (z-score: 4.43)—suggesting a shift in public behavior or increased resident intolerance, possibly linked to outdoor dining or gathering spaces.
evidence: 11 smoking/vaping complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 4.0 weekly average (175% spike)
Z-score of 4.43 indicates statistically significant anomaly, but older than competing spikes
May reflect seasonal behavior (outdoor dining/socializing) rather than acute crisis
reporting_angles: Determine if spike correlates with outdoor dining expansion or seasonal warming
Gather resident quotes on quality-of-life impact in parks or commercial districts
